new_statements.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) There is no contrast in length or tone. Stress is also non-contrastive, occurring on the penultimate syllable of Lihir word forms.
new_statements.citation: Park, Minha & Shinhee Park. 2003. Lihir Organised Phonology Data (Lihir language, Komat dialect). Ukarumpa: SIL Papua New Guinea. Manuscript, 5 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 42375).
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (5 pp., text layer, the PDF's metadata: 'OPD', TSD Linguistics, 2004 PDF of a 2003 draft) opened and fully re-extracted with extracted text. Page 4, under the heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)', reads exactly: 'There is no contrast in length or tone. Stress is also non-contrastive, occurring on the penultimate syllable of Lihir word forms.' -- verbatim as reported (line break aside). Surrounding context: vowel-sequence inventory (/ia ie iee io ioo ua ue uee uo uoo/) immediately before, 'Syllable Patterns' immediately after (V, CV, VC, CVC with syllabifications like pi.tsi.riee, ma.tsieen, a.rieen that treat <iee>/<ieen> as single nuclei -- the other reader's caveat about…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is predictable (non-phonemic) and falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; length and tone are not contrastive.
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned. (Note: the OPD's syllabifications treat orthographic vowel sequences such as <iee>, <uoo> as single nuclei, e.g. ma.tsieen, pi.tsi.riee, which bears on which syllable counts as penultimate.)
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for 'Lihir word forms' (word level); no phrase-level or citation-form discussion. Data are from the Komat dialect, based on 28 months of fieldwork (dated 21 Feb 2003).
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD describes the Komat dialect of Lihir (village Komat, Lihir/Aniolam island group); Glottolog lists no sub-dialect codes under lihi1237, so it maps to lihi1237 directly. Neuhaus (per Schokkin) distinguishes 'light' vs 'dark' (north vs south) dialects.
